subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a stable runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for implementations outside the Node-hosted product runtime?
rationale: This creates a major public architecture, compatibility, security, and long-term versioning commitment that cannot be inferred from the current TypeScript implementation or plugin SDK.

options.title: Define a portable protocol
options.body: Sponsor a versioned schema, platform-capability boundary, and conformance suite for C, Rust, WASM, and embedded implementations.

options.title: Keep Node as the boundary
options.body: Document that projects such as MimiClaw may reuse OpenClaw concepts but are independent implementations rather than protocol-compatible OpenClaw runtimes.

recommendation.title: Define a portable protocol
recommendation.body: Sponsor a versioned schema, platform-capability boundary, and conformance suite for C, Rust, WASM, and embedded implementations.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and central runtime and harness history make this the strongest available owner for the product-boundary decision.
